section: Purpose, loan categories and eligible lenders
source_authority: Department of Financial Services, Government of India
text: The Department of Financial Services states that Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) was launched on 8 April 2015 to provide institutional collateral-free credit to micro enterprises. It covers non-agricultural activities and activities allied to agriculture, including poultry, dairy and beekeeping, and can meet both term-loan and working-capital needs. The official categories are Shishu, up to Rs. 50,000; Kishore, above Rs. 50,000 and up to Rs. 5 lakh; Tarun, above Rs. 5 lakh and up to Rs. 10 lakh; and Tarun Plus, above Rs. 10 lakh and up to Rs. 20 lakh for entrepreneurs who previously obtained and successfully repaid a Tarun-category loan, effective from 24 October 2024. Member lending institutions include public-sector, private-sector and foreign banks, regional rural banks, small finance banks, non-banking financial companies, microfinance institutions and NBFC-MFIs. The page states that collateral is not required.
title: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana - Department of Financial Services
